speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Taxi availability standards were also introduced and taxi operators can grow their fleets by up to 2% per annum, subject to meeting the standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Unlike taxis, PHCs are, essentially, privately-owned cars that have the flexibility and autonomy to take passengers, thereby augmenting our supply of P2P vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Hence, PHCs are treated like privately-owned cars under the vehicle quota system.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: I just have a supplementary question for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: As she has mentioned, in 2012, taxis were removed from the COE bidding system and I think, in July 2016, then Transport Minister Mr Khaw Boon Wan shared that, on PHCs, the Government will monitor its rate of growth and uptake of COEs to see if a similar move will be appropriate.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, in terms of the relevance of PHCs within this P2P sector, it is now much more than that for taxis.

speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
text: So, I am just wondering if the Senior Minister of State and the Ministry will consider having a similar treatment when it comes to COEs for both PHCs and taxis.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have explained in my reply earlier, for PHCs, essentially, they have the autonomy and they have the flexibility to decide if they are going to pick up passengers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, basically, they are like privately-owned cars and if they do take up passengers, it means it helps us supplement the P2P sector in terms of the vehicle population.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But if you are going to put them like taxis into a separate category, as I have mentioned, first of all, there is an additional difficulty because we will then have to have specific requirements like ensuring that they comply with minimum number of trips and that is actually very difficult to enforce.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will add to compliance cost which will, eventually, trickle down to consumers.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But in addition to that, this call or request to review COE categories is actually quite a perennial suggestion.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Essentially, there is a trade-off between having specific categories to meet specific requirements versus ensuring that there is sufficient COE quota for that category.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, whether you have a specific category for PHCs or something else, the fact is that it is going to lead to further fragmentation and volatility, particularly when COE supply is low.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if you are looking at COE premiums and so on, basically, it is, fundamentally, demand-and-supply for vehicles that determines COE premiums.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I have also said, we will continue to monitor the situation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For PHCs, we have been closely watching the market and there is really no evidence that the PHC companies have caused an increase in COE premiums.
